reason: The text explicitly demonstrates that non-leaders possess agency. The passage shows the congregation (עֵדָה - the broader assembly of Israelites, not just leaders) exercising multiple forms of agency: they collectively voice complaints (וַיִּלֹּ֙נוּ֙ עַל־ מֹשֶׁ֣ה), lift up their voices and weep (וַתִּשָּׂא֙ כָּל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַֽיִּתְּנ֖וּ אֶת־ קוֹלָ֑ם), make collective decisions (וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ כָּל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה לִרְגּ֥וֹם אֹתָ֖ם), and attempt to return to Egypt. While leaders like Moses, Joshua, and Caleb also clearly exercise agency, the narrative repeatedly emphasizes the agency of the wider population through their speech, complaints, and attempted actions. The phrase 'all the congregation' (כָּל־ הָעֵדָ֣ה) appears multiple times describing actions taken by the people collectively.
